source_name: Burza cenných papírů Praha (Prague Stock Exchange) — issuer information and market rules
why_relevant: The market operator that defines which issuers sit on Prime, Standard, Free and START markets and what each tier must disclose (Burzovní pravidla). Complements the ČNB registers: OAM covers regulated-market issuers, but START/Free market issuers have exchange-level rather than statutory disclosure duties, so PSE is the only index of that population. Also useful for confirming ISINs and listing status when reconciling the OAM issuer dropdown.

source_name: Sbírka listin — per-entity list of filed documents (annual report, financial statements, auditor's report)
why_relevant: This is the actual disclosure channel of the cell: for a given subjektId it lists every document filed into the collection of deeds, labelled in Czech with the reporting year — 'účetní závěrka [2024]', 'výroční zpráva [2024]', 'zpráva auditora [2024]', 'zpráva o vztazích [2024]' (related-party report). Confirmed on a bank (Komerční banka, subjektId=68415) with an unbroken 2018–2024 series. For unlisted payment institutions, processors and IT suppliers with no IR page and no press releases, this is the only place revenue, equity, auditor identity and intra-group relations are disclosed. The related-party report is the single best public artefact for mapping which group entities supply which bank.

source_name: Úplný výpis z obchodního rejstříku (full historical extract)
why_relevant: The 'úplný výpis' shows the full struck-through history of a company: former trade names, seat moves, share capital increases, changes of statutory bodies, sole-shareholder entries, mergers and branch (odštěpný závod) registrations. This is exactly the pointer behaviour the cell needs — it reveals rebrandings, silent ownership transfers of payment/IT vendors and subsidiary structures that no corporate website lists, and it dates each change.

source_name: Opendata ISVR — bulk open data of the public register (dataor.justice.cz)
why_relevant: Local open-data catalogue of the Ministry of Justice publishing the public register in bulk as XML/CSV, filterable by registry court, legal form and period (coverage stated back to 1900). This is the scalable way to build the CZ banking/payments actor universe — every a.s./s.r.o. with its officers, seat and registration events — without hammering the web UI. Its user manual (81 pages) documents per-legal-form attribute sets (s.r.o., a.s., družstvo, ...).

source_name: Opendata ISVR machine API (CKAN-style action endpoints)
why_relevant: The dataor SPA calls a CKAN-style API (/api/3/action/package_list_compact, /api/3/action/package_show, /api/file/) — i.e. the bulk register data is reachable programmatically rather than only through the browser UI. Worth tracking because it would remove the SPA/headless-browser dependency from the actor-universe pipeline.

source_name: ARES REST API — ekonomicke-subjekty (unauthenticated JSON)
why_relevant: Open, key-free JSON API returning the structured entity record: obchodniJmeno, sidlo, pravniForma, datumVzniku, DIČ, czNace2008 list and a seznamRegistraci block showing which source registers (VR/RES/RŽP/DPH/insolvency/...) hold the subject. A POST /vyhledat search accepts obchodniJmeno and returns paged hits — a live test on the Czech term 'platební' returned 'Platební instituce Roger a.s.' (IČO 01729462). This is the workhorse for building and refreshing the CZ payments actor map, and NACE filtering surfaces suppliers that never call themselves 'payments'.

source_name: Portál otevřených dat Ministerstva financí — ARES datasets and API conditions
why_relevant: MF's open-data portal page for ARES: it documents the REST and legacy XML interfaces, links the 'AresRestApi' JSON specification attachment, and states the operating limits verbatim (blocking above 500 queries/minute, on repeated identical/incorrect queries, on multi-IP limit circumvention, on random database trawling). Required reading to keep the actor-map pipeline lawful and unblocked, and it also points to downloadable ARES datasets.

source_name: Evidence skutečných majitelů (ESM) — beneficial ownership register
why_relevant: The statutory beneficial-ownership register — historically the only free way to see who ultimately controls a Czech payment institution, processor or ATM operator behind holding chains. It remains highly valuable for ownership mapping, but its free public channel has been shut: the Ministry of Justice announced that from 17 December 2025 'Veřejná část ESM a otevřená data budou nedostupná', following Czech Supreme Court / Supreme Administrative Court and CJEU rulings and the 6th AML package. Access now requires login via data box, privileged remote access, or proving legitimate interest to a court.

source_name: Evidence svěřenských fondů (ESF) — register of trusts
why_relevant: Companion register to the commercial register covering svěřenské fondy (Czech trusts), which are a common holding layer above Czech operating companies including fintech/payment vendors. Useful when a payment institution's registered shareholder is a trust rather than a company, i.e. exactly where the commercial register stops explaining ownership.

source_name: Insolvenční rejstřík (ISIR)
why_relevant: Insolvency register run by the same ministry. For this cell it is the negative-signal companion to the deeds collection: it flags payment intermediaries, ATM/cash-handling firms and IT suppliers entering insolvency or reorganisation — an early indicator of a bank's supplier risk, of consolidation opportunities, and of why a filing series suddenly stops.

source_name: Registr živnostenského podnikání (RŽP) — Portál živnostenského podnikání
why_relevant: Trade-licence register. It records the licensed activity scope of a company (e.g. 'Poskytování software, poradenství v oblasti informačních technologií...') and its establishments, and it covers sole traders and small vendors that are in ARES but carry little in the deeds collection. Useful for finding the long tail of POS/IT service suppliers around banks and for confirming what a vendor is actually licensed to do.

source_name: Registr ekonomických subjektů (RES) — Czech Statistical Office search
why_relevant: The statistical register behind ARES's RES layer. Its distinctive added value for this cell is the employee-size band and the institutional-sector/NACE classification for entities that file only abbreviated accounts — i.e. a size proxy for small payment and IT vendors whose deeds filings disclose almost no P&L detail.

source_name: Registr plátců DPH (ADIS) — VAT payer register, Financial Administration
why_relevant: VAT registration register showing registration/deregistration dates, unreliable-payer status and published bank accounts. A weak but cheap health and continuity signal on payment-sector suppliers, and a way to date when a newly incorporated fintech actually started trading.

source_name: Národní katalog otevřených dat (NKOD) — data.gov.cz
why_relevant: National open-data catalogue that indexes the datasets published by the Ministry of Justice (ISVR), Ministry of Finance (ARES), ČSÚ and others. The right place to discover new or replacement bulk distributions when a ministry moves or re-publishes a register, and to see each dataset's declared licence.

source_name: ČNB — seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů (JERRS)
why_relevant: Czech National Bank's register of licensed and registered financial-market entities. It is the authoritative way to enumerate which CZ entities are banks, payment institutions, small-scale payment service providers, e-money institutions or their agents — and it carries IČO, which is the join key into the commercial register and ARES. Used as the seeding list, the deeds collection then supplies each of those entities' annual accounts.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal — Business Registers Interconnection (BRIS)
why_relevant: EU-level search across national business registers, including the Czech one. Its value for this cell is cross-border: when a CZ payment institution or processor is a subsidiary of a Slovak, Austrian, German or Polish parent, BRIS lets you follow the chain into the parent's home register (and its filings) without knowing each national portal.

source_name: Kurzy.cz — Rejstřík firem / Sbírka listin mirror
why_relevant: Large Czech financial portal that mirrors the commercial register and indexes the collection of deeds per company, often with parsed financial highlights and a cleaner, non-CAPTCHA HTML surface than or.justice.cz. Useful as a redundancy path and for quick human lookups, but it is a derivative of the official register and can lag or mis-parse, so the official filing remains the source of truth.

source_name: Peníze.cz — Obchodní rejstřík / rejstřík firem
why_relevant: Another well-established Czech register aggregator, notable for rendering ownership and officer relationship graphs and for surfacing extracted financial statement values per year. Helpful for fast triage of a payments vendor's size and connections before deciding whether to pull the underlying filings.

source_name: Merk.cz (Imper) — company database with parsed účetní závěrky
why_relevant: Commercial company database that parses filed financial statements into structured indicators (revenue trend, profitability, indebtedness, creditworthiness) and person-company links. Its dedicated 'Účetní závěrky' section is effectively a structured layer over the same deeds filings this cell targets — valuable when you need many CZ vendors' revenue series without building your own PDF extraction.

source_name: CRIBIS (CRIF) — Czech credit and company information service
why_relevant: Paid credit-information service built on the register, deeds filings, insolvency and payment-behaviour data. The realistic route to comprehensive, normalised financials and group structures for hundreds of CZ payment/IT vendors at once, including entities whose PDF filings are scanned and hard to parse.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet Czech Republic (formerly Bisnode / Albertina)
why_relevant: The old Bisnode.cz and Albertina.cz Czech data brands now redirect to Dun & Bradstreet's Czech site — i.e. the historic Albertina/Bisnode CZ company-data franchise is the same vendor today. Relevant as the main international provider of normalised Czech company financials, ownership trees and DUNS-linked group structures, and as one of the few places likely to retain pre-December-2025 beneficial-ownership snapshots.

source_name: Hlídač státu — open data and API over Czech state sources (incl. justice/ISIR)
why_relevant: Civic-tech platform that republishes Czech state datasets — including justice-sector and insolvency data — as documented APIs under an open licence (CC BY). Valuable as a pre-normalised, automation-friendly alternative to hammering the ministry's own UIs, and as a monitor of which state registers publish properly as open data.

source_name: Chytrý rejstřík — commercial register with revenue and risk overlays
why_relevant: Aggregator positioning itself around 'tržby, rizika, vozidla, kontakty' and publishing explainers on exactly what the collection of deeds contains (financial statements, annual reports). Useful as a secondary index and, in particular, as a Czech-language reference for how filings are structured and labelled.

source_name: Obchodnirejstrik.cz — independent register search
why_relevant: Long-running independent Czech register search site. Low unique value over the official register, but a useful fallback index and a source of alternate company-name spellings when the official search is strict about diacritics and legal-form suffixes.

source_name: Komerční banka – EUR covered bond (debt investor page: base prospectus, final terms, investor reports, HTT)
why_relevant: Best-in-class Czech covered-bond debt-investor page and the model for the whole cell. Observed inventory: EUR 5bn mortgage covered bond base prospectus (Oct 2025 and Jan 2021 editions) plus a First Supplement dated 31 March 2026; final terms per tranche incl. ISIN XS3401900173 / XS3401900256 (June 2026) and 2025/2021 issues; quarterly Covered Bond Investor Reports for two cover pools (KB_EUR_HZL_0001 and KB_HZL_0000, latest observed as of 30 June 2026); quarterly HTT Covered Bond Label reporting in XLSX; a Fitch AAA rating action link; and a redemption notice for XS2289128162. The HTT XLSX is machine-readable cover-pool data — LTV bands, seasoning, regional split, OC — that appears nowhere in KB's annual report.

source_name: Komerční banka – Informace o cenných papírech (povinně uveřejňované informace)
why_relevant: KB's Czech-language mandatory-disclosure hub for securities. Observed: a rate table (updated 24 July 2026) of ISIN / yield period / coupon 2.00–6.47% p.a. for outstanding HZL KB issues; notices to bondholders (EUR covered bond issuances of 2 Apr 2026 and 9 Oct 2025, nominal-value notifications, redemption and buyback notices); traded issues such as HZL KB 3,125%/2033 (XS3401900173) and HZL KB 2,750%/2030 (XS3203038347); base prospectuses for the EUR 5bn covered bond programme and the legacy KB II bond programme. It also carries a large archive of client/corporate bond programmes KB arranges — a side channel into Czech corporate funding.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank a.s. – Emise cenných papírů Raiffeisenbank (base prospectuses, final terms, sustainable-bond impact reports)
why_relevant: RBCZ's own debt-issuance disclosure page. Observed: four generations of the 'Raiffeisenbank a.s. EUR 5 bln Note Bond Programme' base prospectus (Nov 2020, Sep 2022, Apr 2024, and a 24 June 2026 update), multiple final terms / emisní podmínky for subordinated and senior non-preferred bonds in CZK and EUR with ISINs and coupon notices, annual Impact and Allocation Reports for its sustainable bond (2021–2025), and a reference to an International Covered Bonds Programme. RBCZ holds two covered blocks (RBCZ_BLOCK_02, RBCZ_BLOCK_03) per the ČNB register, so this page is the primary route to its covered-bond documentation.

source_name: UniCredit Bank CZ&SK – International €10 bln Covered Bond Programme (programme page + base prospectuses)
why_relevant: Dedicated programme page for the International EUR 10bn Covered Bond Programme. Indexed content shows it hosts Cover Pool Information (for LCR purposes), HTT Covered Bond Label reporting, a Planned Covered Bond Issuance investor presentation, and the Base Prospectus dated 16 September 2024, alongside older editions (e.g. a 10 January 2017 base prospectus under the earlier €5bn programme). This is the deepest non-annual-report disclosure UCB CZ&SK makes about its Czech mortgage book.

source_name: MONETA Money Bank – Bonds (investors.moneta.cz/bonds)
why_relevant: Full capital-stack debt disclosure in one place, unusually complete for a mid-cap Czech bank. Observed: AT1 prospectus (ISIN XS3402816162, June 2026); Tier 2 base prospectus (XS3154053436, Sep 2025) and legacy T2 final terms (CZ0003704918, CZ0003705188); senior preferred/unsecured prospectuses (XS2898794982 Sep 2024, XS2435601443 Feb 2022, CZ0003707671 Nov 2022); a covered-bond base prospectus (18 Sep 2023) with final terms for HZL MONETA 4,97/26 (CZ0002009012) and HZL MONETA 4,83/27 (CZ0002009020); recurring Cover Pool Overviews through June 2026 (Czech only); and the historical Wüstenrot hypoteční banka Bond Programme II archive. Because MONETA is listed, this sits alongside equity IR but the documents themselves are pure debt-investor material.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Dokumenty ke stažení, sekce Dluhopisy a MREL
why_relevant: ČS's IR hub (Pro akcionáře a investory) routes debt investors to a dedicated 'Dluhopisy a MREL' bucket inside its document library. ČS holds covered block CSHZL2 in the ČNB register, joined the Covered Bond Label as the third Czech issuer, and per third-party research published its first HTT-standard report as of 31 March 2026 covering a cover pool of CZK 308.5bn (EUR 12.6bn) of fixed-rate domestic mortgages. Its inaugural EUR 500m mortgage covered bond was Moody's Aaa-rated and listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange regulated market. This is the largest Czech mortgage book and the highest-value cover-pool disclosure in the country.

source_name: Hypoteční banka / ČSOB Hypoteční banka – document store (základní prospekt dluhopisového programu, emisní dodatky HZL)
why_relevant: Hypoteční banka (formerly Českomoravská hypoteční banka, ČSOB group, covered block HB-Blok 4) has been the country's oldest and largest HZL issuer, issuing continuously since 1996. Its third bond programme, established 2013, runs 30 years and each tranche is documented by an emisní dodatek. Indexed documents include the 3rd programme base prospectus (versions dated 13 July 2018 and 14 April 2019) and emission supplements such as the 25th HZL issue. ČSOB group discloses very little of its Czech mortgage book to equity investors, so this prospectus/supplement trail is the main window.

source_name: Hypoteční banka – tiskové zprávy, rubrika Emise HZL
why_relevant: Dedicated press-release category for HZL issuance — the announcement layer that dates each tranche and often names the placement channel (e.g. issues placed with ČSOB Private Banking clients rather than institutional books). Useful as a low-latency trigger to go look for the corresponding emisní dodatek, and it reveals distribution strategy that prospectuses do not state plainly.

source_name: Covered Bond Label (ECBC/EMF) – issuer directory, HTT database and national information
why_relevant: Cross-jurisdiction aggregator that normalises cover-pool disclosure into the Harmonised Transparency Template. Three Czech issuers are labelled: Komerční banka (first Czech issuer to obtain the Label), UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia (issuer id 214), and Česká spořitelna (third Czech joiner). The site exposes an issuer directory (/issuers/directory), national information (/issuers/national/list), recently published HTTs (/new-htt), a cover-pool comparison tool (/htt-database), label statistics (/bonds) and a legislative comparative database. It is the fastest way to detect a new Czech HTT filing and to compare Czech cover pools against peers.

source_name: ECBC / EMF-ECBC – European Covered Bond Fact Book (Czech Republic chapter)
why_relevant: Annual reference work with a standing Czech Republic country chapter written by Czech market practitioners (a recent edition credits Pavel Kühn of Česká spořitelna). It sets out the legal basis — Act No. 190/2004 Coll. on Bonds as amended, and the Czech implementation of the EU Covered Bond Directive — the HZL definition, cover-pool eligibility, OC rules, outstanding volumes and issuer list. It is the fastest way to get an authoritative baseline of the Czech covered-bond framework and to date-stamp legal changes, without reading the statute.

source_name: NORD/LB Floor Research – Covered Bond & SSA View (weekly) and covered-bond research archive
why_relevant: Free, weekly sell-side research that repeatedly runs CEE and Czech/Slovak covered-bond focus pieces. Editions retrieved in this run carry issuer-level Czech detail not published by the issuers themselves in that form — e.g. Česká spořitelna's first HTT report as of 31 March 2026 with a CZK 308.5bn (EUR 12.6bn) all-fixed-rate domestic mortgage cover pool, ČS market shares (retail loans 26.9%, retail deposits 23.5%), KB's new covered-bond programme launch, and the observation that Czechia/Hungary/Poland favour domestic-currency covered bonds while Slovakia moves to EUR benchmarks. Excellent for interpretation and for catching issuance before it hits official registers.

source_name: ČNB – Kritéria přijatelnosti pro hypoteční zástavní listy (HZL) a nastavení haircutů
why_relevant: Central-bank eligibility criteria and haircuts for accepting HZL as collateral in ČNB liquidity-providing repo operations. This is a revealed-preference source: it tells you which covered bonds the central bank will finance, on what terms, and therefore which HZL are genuinely liquid instruments versus retained/self-held paper. Changes to haircuts or eligibility are a leading indicator of funding-condition shifts for Czech mortgage lenders.

source_name: ČNB – Obecný přístup ke stanovení minimálního požadavku na kapitál a způsobilé závazky (MREL) a sekce Řešení krize
why_relevant: ČNB as resolution authority publishes its general methodology for setting MREL — 2*(P1+P2) for large/systemically important/complex banks earmarked for bail-in, and (P1+P2) + coefficient*(P1+P2) for mid-sized, less complex banks resolved via transfer to a private acquirer — plus transition periods and an aggregate estimate that banks would need to add roughly CZK 120–140bn. ČNB explicitly does not publish bank-by-bank MREL values, so this methodology page is the only public way to reverse-engineer why and when a given Czech bank must come to market with senior non-preferred or subordinated paper. It is the demand driver behind most non-covered bank issuance in this cell.

source_name: Banka CREDITAS – emise dluhopisů (MREL) infoletters and prospectus programme
why_relevant: Challenger-bank corner of the cell, and a useful contrast case: CREDITAS funds MREL in CZK through the retail/domestic channel rather than EUR benchmarks. Retrieved facts include a CZK 1bn three-year MREL issue (CREDITAS 7,50/27, CZK 10,000 nominal, 7.5% fixed, maturity 30 July 2027, issuer call after two years, admitted to the Prague Stock Exchange regulated market), and a June 2024 prospectus permitting up to CZK 20bn of issuance with a first CZK 750m issue under a CZK 2bn programme. Small banks disclose funding cost and capital plans here that never appear elsewhere.

source_name: Burza cenných papírů Praha (Prague Stock Exchange) – Bonds / Debt securities market and Issuers' Guide
why_relevant: Listing venue for CZK-denominated bank paper, including HZL and CZK MREL issues (e.g. CREDITAS 7,50/27). PSE segments bond trading by Corporate / Public / Financial / Other sector and publishes admission conditions for the Official and Regulated Markets, trading rules, and 'Parameters of Issues'. Admission requires a prospectus plus three years of financial statements and a Central Depository registration confirmation, and issuers commit to ongoing disclosure in Czech, Slovak or English. The financial-sector bond list is a compact way to enumerate outstanding listed Czech bank debt.

source_name: Centrální depozitář cenných papírů (CDCP) – Seznam vydaných ISINů
why_relevant: Czech CSD publishes a searchable list of ISINs it has assigned since 1 July 2010, searchable by ISIN and by IČO. For this cell it is the authoritative resolver for domestic CZ-prefixed bank bond and HZL identifiers (e.g. CZ0002009012 / CZ0002009020 for MONETA HZL, CZ0003xxxxx for senior/subordinated paper) — the counterpart to the XS/AT identifiers used for international issues. Also publishes an operating manual and an annual Fact Book with issuance statistics.

source_name: Erste Group Bank AG – Debt Investors / Download-Centre (group-level context for Česká spořitelna)
why_relevant: ČS is an Erste Group subsidiary and Erste runs a full debt-investor franchise with a product overview (mortgage covered bonds, public-sector covered bonds, senior instruments), cover-pool reporting and a download centre of finance reports and statements. Group-level MREL strategy, issuance plans and CEE funding commentary set the frame within which ČS's own Czech covered-bond programme operates, and Erste presentations often disclose ČS funding and mortgage-book figures.

source_name: Cbonds – Czech bank issuer and bond reference pages
why_relevant: Commercial bond-market database with per-issuer and per-ISIN pages for Czech bank paper, carrying identifiers (ISIN, FIGI, WKN), coupon, maturity, currency and rating history. Retrieved examples for Česká spořitelna alone span EUR, USD and perpetual CZK instruments (XS2676413235, XS2555412001, XS2638560156, XS2746647036, XS2852933329, XS2930541698, AT0000A2STV4, CZ0003704769) — an inventory that is far quicker to assemble here than by walking every issuer site. The AT-prefixed identifier is a useful hint that some ČS paper is issued/listed via Austrian infrastructure.

source_name: Hypoindex.cz – tiskové zprávy / rubrika emise hypotečních zástavních listů
why_relevant: Czech mortgage-market trade portal that reprints bank press releases about HZL issues, often with volume, coupon and target investor group, and provides a running commentary on which banks are leaning on covered-bond funding in a given month. Useful as a low-cost early-warning feed and as an archive of older HZL issues (multiple Česká spořitelna HZL announcements of CZK 2bn/4bn/5bn were surfaced this way) that the banks themselves have since removed from their sites.

source_name: J&T Banka a Fio banka – komentáře k emisím MREL dluhopisů (broker research notes / zprávy z burzy)
why_relevant: Czech brokers publish short, dated notes on each domestic MREL/SNP issue, frequently ahead of or alongside the formal filing, and give pricing colour that issuers omit. Retrieved examples cover Banka CREDITAS MREL issues at 7.5% and MONETA's MREL programme — including a CZK 1.5bn issue at an 8% coupon, a mandate for a EUR 300m six-year non-call-five MREL bond at 4.41% p.a., nine-times oversubscription, bookrunners BNP Paribas and JPMorgan with Goldman Sachs Bank Europe and J&T Banka as co-managers, and the resulting +453bp move in MREL ratio to 28.23% against a 22.45% management target. That level of transaction detail is not in any prospectus.

source_name: Fitch Ratings – Czech covered bond rating actions (e.g. Komerční banka soft bullet covered bonds)
why_relevant: Rating agency covered-bond commentary carries the analytics behind a programme — OC levels relied upon, D-Cap/discontinuity assessment, cover-pool credit assumptions, refinancing spreads — that neither the prospectus nor the HTT states as a judgement. KB's programme is rated AAA (Stable) by Fitch as of 24 June 2026; Česká spořitelna's inaugural covered bond was Moody's Aaa. Rating actions are also the most reliable public signal that a programme has changed materially.

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (Ministerstvo spravedlnosti ČR) + Justice open data
why_relevant: Statutory filing archive: every stavební spořitelna, spořitelní družstvo, penzijní společnost and obchodník s cennými papíry must file its účetní závěrka, výroční zpráva and auditor's report into the Sbírka listin. This is the fallback of record whenever an entity's own website hides, moves or prunes its annual reports (and the only reliable route for the smaller credit unions, which publish irregularly). dataor.justice.cz offers bulk open data for the register itself, enabling IČO-driven automated retrieval.

source_name: Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna, a.s. – Dokumenty / Povinně uveřejňované informace a výroční zprávy
why_relevant: Best-structured building-society disclosure library found in this cell: bilingual annual reports (Výroční zpráva RSTS / Annual Report RSTS) confirmed for 2020–2025 as PDFs, plus a large archive of quarterly regulatory filings spanning 2020–2026. RSTS sits inside the Raiffeisen group in CZ and its entity-level report exposes branch/advisor network, distribution mix and IT/digitalisation spend that the group consolidated report aggregates away — exactly the channel-and-technology signal this cell exists to capture.

source_name: ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, a.s. (ex-Českomoravská stavební spořitelna / ČMSS „Liška“) – Výroční zprávy
why_relevant: Largest Czech building society by tradition, now 100% owned by ČSOB (KBC) after ČSOB bought out Bausparkasse Schwäbisch Hall's 45% stake in 2019 and rebranded from ČMSS. Its standalone annual report documents the post-acquisition channel migration (own advisor network vs ČSOB branches, self-service and digital onboarding) at an entity level the KBC/ČSOB consolidated report does not break out. A separate page carries the ČNB-decree disclosures.
